lines.trans: I'm going to film you right here as we are, alright?
May I ask one thing? What is your favorite color?
Black.
Alright — then starting today, you are Kuroki. Kaoru Kuroki.
Bare everything you have; my videos are filmed for real.
What else could there possibly be? Please look closely — this is who I am.
Hey, if she shaves her underarms it won't be an issue.
I have no wish to shave them.
There is zero need to shave — they are truly wonderful.
That makes me happy. Starting today, I become Kaoru Kuroki.
Stop the camera for now — I changed my mind.

words.gram: Plain imperative of くれる (give/do for me).
Noun in the idiom 気が向く (feel like doing).

meanings.note: Directly modifies a noun near the speaker (この店, この辺, この部分).

examples.text: この本は人気があります。

meanings.note: Second-person pronoun used by superiors, in songs/books, or between close friends.

examples.text: 君の意見はどうですか。
君ならきっとできるよ。

meanings.note: Written を and pronounced o; marks what an action directly acts upon.
Tells the listener something new or adds warm reassurance at the end of a sentence.
Irregular i-adjective whose past/conditional stems use よ- (よかったら).

examples.text: よかったら来てください。

meanings.note: Checks agreement ('isn't it?') or softens a request or farewell.
Native Japanese counter for general objects and abstract things like reasons.

examples.text: 理由がもう一つあります。
りんごを一つください。

meanings.note: Turns a statement into a question, or softens a volitional/negative guess.
Na-adjective; the thing liked is marked with が or は.

examples.text: どんな食べ物が好きですか。
examples.trans: What kind of food do you like?

meanings.en: casual reflection or firm reminder particle
meanings.note: Used aloud to oneself ('man, I'm hungry') or at the end of a warning ('remember that, okay?').

meanings.en: as for; topic or contrast marker
meanings.note: Written は but pronounced wa when marking the topic or contrasting one item with another.
Satisfied exclamation when gearing up or finishing a task cleanly.
Contracts では; launches a decision ('well then') or opens casual farewell じゃあね.
Special reading きょう.
Follows a clause to give a reason or reassuring explanation.

examples.trans: Because it is close, I walk.

meanings.note: Plain sentence-ending copula; contracts or shifts to だった in past, だろう/だろ for supposition, and で/じゃ in combinations.
Used adverbially or as a noun to mean 'everything' or 'all of them'.

examples.text: すべてうまくいきました。
俺は死ぬ気でお前と向かい合ってる。受け止めてやるからすべてさらけ出せ。
examples.trans: I'm facing you with everything on the line; I'll catch whatever you give, so bare it all.

examples.text: 現場でよく聞く言葉だ。
examples.trans: It's an expression often heard on set.

examples.text: お前ら、観光じゃないんだからしっかりしろよ。
examples.trans: Hey, this isn't sightseeing, so pull yourselves together.

examples.text: 彼女は来るんだろうな？
ちゃんとキャストはそろってるんだろうな？
examples.trans: You've got the whole cast properly lined up, right?

meanings.note: Used among friends and peers by men; switch to 私 or 僕 in formal settings.
Links a modifying noun to a following noun, or turns a clause into an explanatory statement (often contracted to ん in speech).
In casual speech, それ plus は often fuses into そりゃ ('well, as for that / of course').
Read なん before だ/です/の, and なに before が/を or alone.

examples.text: 何を買いにきましたか。
examples.trans: What did you come to buy?

meanings.note: Marks the subject of existence, emergence, or questions (どれが), and at the end of a polite clause softens a request (のですが).

examples.text: お願いがあるのですが。
examples.trans: I have a favor to ask.

meanings.en: exist; be available; remain in place
meanings.note: Used for inanimate things and abstract concepts; after て-form (書いてある, 置いてある) describes a resulting state left in place.

examples.text: 名前が書いてあります。

meanings.note: Reassures that rules or steps are followed properly.

examples.text: ちゃんと確認しました。
ちゃんと並んでいます。

meanings.note: Ichidan verb: blunt imperative 見ろ ('look!') is rough command speech.
Follows a verb's て-form or polite お + stem (お待ちください, お持ち帰りください) to make a polite request.

examples.text: ここに書いてください。

meanings.note: Standalone pronoun ('this'), unlike この which requires a noun.
Standard gender-neutral 'I' in polite and business Japanese.
Polite sentence-ending counterpart of plain だ.

cells: ではありません / じゃありません

meanings.note: Softens a refusal or correction at the start of a reply.

examples.text: いや、剃れば問題ねえよ。
examples.trans: Hey, if she shaves her underarms it won't be an issue.
I have no wish to shave them.

examples.text: 剃る必要はない。すごくすてきだ。
examples.trans: There is zero need to shave — they are truly wonderful.

meanings.note: Used for social/work issues as well as test questions.

examples.text: それは大きな問題です。
特に問題はありません。

meanings.note: Polite/dialectal negative ending, especially in ～ません.
Used with が before it (ストーリーが必要だ 'a story is needed') or な before a noun.
Marks the presence of a person (責任者はいるか) or follows て-form (often contracted to てる/てます in speech).
Plain い-adjective.

examples.text: 彼の英語は本当にすごい。

meanings.note: All-purpose action verb; turns Sino-Japanese nouns into verbs (融通する, 出店する) and with に means 'decide on' or 'make into'.

meanings.en: come; go do something and return (after て-form)
meanings.note: Written in kana after a て-form (話してきます), expresses stepping away to do an action and coming back.

examples.text: ちょっと水を買ってきます。
examples.trans: I will go buy some water and be right back.

meanings.en: target, location of existence, or result marker
meanings.note: Marks destination, location where something exists or sits, or the chosen result before する and なる.
Expresses change of state, or in polite customer service (になります) states an arrangement or price total.

examples.trans: That comes to one thousand yen.

meanings.en: do a favor for the speaker
meanings.note: After a te-form (会ってくれる？), warmly asks 'will you do that for us?'

examples.trans: Will you come again for me?

examples.text: 母が料理を作ってくれました。
examples.trans: My mother cooked food for me.

できる.gloss: be built; open; be able to

meanings.en: come into existence; be completed; can do
meanings.note: With buildings or stores (店ができる), means a new shop has been built or opened.

examples.text: 駅前に新しいカフェができました。
examples.trans: A new café opened in front of the station.

examples.text: 日本語が少しできます。
examples.trans: I can speak a little Japanese.

meanings.note: Used in everyday farewells like またね, また明日, and また会いましょう.

examples.text: また明日会いましょう。

meanings.note: Everyday reading あした; pairs with また in また明日 ('see you tomorrow').
